Soojin — quick answers to the procurement points below (draft language):

1) Uptime SLO definition: "Redwood measures availability as the percentage of successful API requests (2xx application-level responses) over a rolling 30-day window. Scheduled maintenance windows communicated 72+ hours in advance are excluded. Availability SLO: 99.9% (monthly equivalent), measured on a rolling 30-day basis for production endpoints."

2) Latency SLOs: "We publish p95 and p99 serving latency for text generation and embeddings. Latency is computed per-tenant (customer API key) and aggregated across our serving fleet; percentile calculations use request-level end-to-end latency excluding queued/dropped requests. Typical baseline: p95 < 300ms, p99 < 900ms for our standard small model family (subject to model selection)."

3) Alerting thresholds: "Customer-facing alerts: availability < SLO for 2 consecutive 5-minute evaluation windows or error budget burn > 20% within a 24-hour period. Internal paging uses more sensitive thresholds (error spike > 5% absolute in 5m)."

4) Dashboard & exports: "Customers can be granted read-only Grafana dashboards scoped to their tenant. We provide time-series exports (CSV) on request and Prometheus-compatible metrics via a secure pull for enterprise plans. Live Grafana access can be provisioned within 48 hours once tenant linkage is complete."

5) Retention: "High-resolution metrics retained for 90 days, downsampled metrics retained for 2 years. Raw request logs retained for 90 days by default; longer retention available on dedicated/private contracts. Exports for audit purposes are supported via secure S3 transfer or shared Drive link."

I'll attach the SLO template and a short monitoring runbook. Marked items where we might need legal sign-off (rolling window vs calendar month).

Adding the exception & operational notes for procurement packet:

- Exception requests: we allow temporary SLO exceptions (e.g., planned migration or bulk onboarding) with a documented exception request that includes start/end times, expected impact, and mitigation plan. Exceptions are tracked and must be approved by the reliability team; typical turn-around 2 business days.
- Data sampling and aggregation: for very high-volume tenants we sample traces at 1% by default for detailed tracing; percentiles are computed on unsampled request-level metrics to avoid bias.
- Dashboards: read-only Grafana for standard enterprise; dedicated customers may get a copy of their dashboards in their VPC.
- Audit artifacts: we can provide a CSV export of per-tenant latency and availability slices for any 30-day window upon request; for procurement evidence we typically provide a 90-day slice of p95/p99 + uptime calculations.

I'll attach the runbook and a filled example SLO spreadsheet (template + example).

-Ben
